title: Чужое парковочное место  (Someone Else's Parking Spot)

segments.t: Out in the courtyard, a parking attendant tells Chef Barinov that his usual spot is taken because an important guest paid extra to park there. Eager to stand up for his boss, Max marches over to tell the driver off, only to realize too late that he has just insulted a powerful friend of the restaurant.
Извините, но в данный момент ваше место занято.
Между прочим, это он занял ваше место.

'You knew it was mine.' The meaning hinges on 'you' working together with 'knew' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'And for how many years now.' The grammar packs 'both' and 'year' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'In short.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'short' and finishing on 'short'.
'I understand, everything is fine.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'understand' in a few short words. Max answers right away.
'A man drove up and paid for it.' Max anchors the line on 'and', while 'to pay' completes the thought.
'What an unexpected meeting.' Notice how Russian expresses 'what' and 'a meeting' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'And what are you doing here?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'and' and finishing on 'are you doing'. Chef Viktor answers right away.

'I will handle it myself, Chef.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'chef' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Max answers right away.
'Damn, I screwed up again.' The meaning hinges on 'darn' working together with 'to screw up' in spoken Russian.
'How was I supposed to know?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'where from' before landing on 'to know'. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
